How this was put together

The numbers on this page are filled in by the build, so they change when the data does.

A "not published" column stays in the tables, empty, with a status field next to it. That way the join is already in place on the day someone publishes the number, and nobody mistakes a blank for a zero.

The City's budget rows

I read the City's two current documents from the public pages of its People's Budget Portal: the enacted 2026 budget (430 rows, ₱1,664.7 million) and the proposed 2027 Annual Investment Program (424 rows, ₱8,698.4 million). (The 2026 overview page's headline is ₱2.12 billion; the difference is ₱457.66 million of special purpose appropriations, which that page states but the Browse page doesn't list.) The Browse page of each carries every published row with its AIP reference code, office, and PS/MOOE/CO split. For the rows of eight offices (education, early childhood, nutrition, child welfare, the library, the science centre and the city college), I also read each row's own page, which lists its funds.

(I help build that portal through Stride Technologies, which is exactly why I kept to the pages any resident's browser receives. The portal's bulk open-data API is switched off for both years by the City's choice, so I didn't use it, and nothing here comes from the admin side.)

Each row then gets a domain from a short list of rules. The first rule that matches wins, and its ID is kept on the row as tag_rule:

The explorer's default total counts basic education, early childhood (eccd), child nutrition, child welfare, library and literacy. In the 2027 AIP that comes to ₱278.7 million across 24 rows, and in the enacted 2026 budget to ₱30.4 million across 23 rows. Those two aren't comparable as a trend: the 2027 figure includes the SEF row and the 2026 one can't (see below).

0 of 47 of those rows name a school or a barangay. Every one is city-wide, so place_level is "city" throughout and each row is listed on the checks page as unplaced.

The SEF

In the 2027 AIP, the Special Education Fund appears as a single row: "Management of the Special Education Fund and Secretariat Support to the Naga City School Board", ₱130,000,000, all of it MOOE, funded by the SEF. That one row is 47% of the education and early-childhood total, and it names no school.

The enacted 2026 rows on the portal carry no fund field at all, and none of them is the SEF. The SEF has its own budget, prepared with the Local School Board, and the portal doesn't carry it. So for 2026 I can't put a peso figure on the SEF from public data.

DepEd's own files fill in part of the picture from the school side. In SY 2023-24, Naga's public schools reported 28 staff paid from the City SEF (2 of them teachers, the rest mostly learning support aides and administrative staff) at 9 schools, plus 23 paid from other LGU funds, and 306 ICT items (mostly TVs and printers) at 37 schools bought with LGU or SEF money. The 2027 SEF row has no PS at all, while the schools report SEF-paid staff. Those are different years and possibly different accounting, so I'd bring it to the City School Board as a question.

DepEd's school data

DepEd publishes school-level files under Project Bukas on its machine-ready files page. I take every school whose division is "Naga City": 98 in SY 2025-26, of which 45 are public, 52 private and one a state college. The public schools sit in 4 school districts and enrol 47,176 learners (2,926 in kindergarten).

From the SY 2023-24 files I take instructional classrooms, buildings needing major repair (or marked for condemnation or demolition), makeshift rooms, staff by funding source, and ICT equipment by funding source. 42 of the 45 public schools appear in those files; the 6 schools that don't (new schools, or new IDs) keep blanks and are listed as gaps.

DepEd's CSVs mix two text encodings, sometimes within one file, so school names like "Concepcion Pequeña" arrive garbled. The pipeline repairs each cell's encoding and leaves the numbers alone.

Reading results

DepEd's machine-ready CRLA 2025-26 file has 6,121 schools, all from CAR, Region I, Region III, Region IX, Region VIII. None is in Bicol, so 0 of Naga's 45 public schools have a reading result I can join. ELLNA and NAT are the same: selected schools elsewhere. The Paaralang Bukas dashboard shows more, but as an embedded report with no download I could find.

The Evidence for Education Coalition cites Naga's City School Board using Project Bukas data to realign the SEF towards remediation and furniture, after which the share of low emerging readers fell from 40% to 4%. That was Naga's own work, done by hand, and the school-level numbers behind it aren't in the public files yet.

ECCD indicators

I looked for barangay-level stunting (Operation Timbang Plus), child development centres (CBMS) and CRLA for Naga. EDCOM 2's Early Childhood Dashboard has the right indicators, but its page sits behind a bot check, and I found no download or API (I didn't try to get past the check). I found no barangay-level OPT+ or CBMS file for Naga either.

So barangays.csv has the three columns, empty, each with a status of "not published", keyed by PSGC code. If EDCOM 2 or the City can share those tables, they drop straight in.

Places

Barangays come from PSA's 2026 PSGC (as parsed by bendlikeabamboo/barangay, tag v2026.10.12.0): Naga has 27. Each school's barangay name from DepEd is matched to a PSGC code after folding case and accents. 98 of 98 schools match. Two names needed a hand match (DepEd's "Concepcion Pequeno" is PSGC's "Concepcion Pequeña"; DepEd's "San Francisco (Pob.)" is PSGC's "San Francisco"), which affects 10 schools; each is listed on the checks page so the match can be checked. 19 of the 27 barangays have a public school.

Boundaries are faeldon's philippines-json-maps v1.1.1, medium resolution. The map is drawn as plain SVG, with no tile server, so the site makes no third-party requests at all.

Checks and gaps

For each budget document, the rows must add up to the total the page itself states, and each row's PS, MOOE, FE and CO must add up to its total. 4 of 4 checks pass. Everything that couldn't be joined, or has no public source, is a row in gaps.csv (216 rows). The checks page lists them all.

What to keep in mind

An appropriation is permission to spend. What was actually paid out sits in the City's accountability reports, which aren't here. The years don't line up either: the budget is FY 2026 and 2027, enrollment is SY 2025-26, and staff, ICT and facilities are SY 2023-24. DepEd's figures are what schools reported through its information systems, as published. DepEd's ICT files lump "LGU or SEF" together, so those items can't be split by fund.

Rerun it
uv run python -m pipeline.fetch     # DepEd files, PSGC, boundaries, the City's portal pages
uv run python -m pipeline.build     # tables, checks, gaps, API, OpenAPI, data package
uv run python -m pipeline.site      # this page and the proposal
uv run python -m pipeline.test_pipeline
